independent_numerical_mutations.description: Random finite binary64 three-factor product differences against exact Fraction.from_float arithmetic.
Independent high-precision Decimal sign and zero oracle on a subset of random binary64 product differences.
Constructed near-cancellation products using the correctly rounded product and adjacent binary64 neighbors.
Exchange antisymmetry and exactly representable common power-of-two scaling properties.
Different exact dyadic factorizations of equal products.
Subnormal tie and overflow-neighborhood rounding, including 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0, 1.5 and 2.5 times minimum subnormal and max plus powers 2^968 through 2^971.
Positive exact-D bounded and unbounded local high-wavenumber branches over random finite binary64 factors and wavenumbers.
Public coefficient, group, criterion, D, high-k, scale, root, matching, classification and Routh entry fuzz over finite binary64 inputs.
Invalid bool, string, Decimal, complex, array, mapping and object admission probes across public scalar and array entries.

p2_findings.finding: Residual, reconstruction, conditioned-sign, Routh-Hurwitz, matching, low-C and analytical representability controls remain candidate numerical policies.
Exact Python-integer arithmetic and Fraction-to-binary64 conversion were independently replayed only in the recorded CPython and Windows runtime.
An exact nonzero D that rounds to binary64 zero fails closed by design; the representability and caller-handling policy has not received separate API or tolerance authority.
The inherited companion-QZ path may fail closed for ill-scaled high-wavenumber or extreme-rate polynomials and has no independently frozen Bai tolerance authority.
The candidate receipt reports the 358-test related regression without directly hash-binding the five auxiliary test files and their complete implementation dependency set.
Several manuscript-context files use the label Bai amendment V2 while the numerical scalar reference is V5; the namespaces are reconcilable but not explicitly distinguished everywhere.
V5 is a scalar reference only and does not embed the HCP operator, prove strict HCP-to-Bai reduction, establish the full HCP high-k Schur cutoff, compare nonlinear UEL growth, or validate TA2.

allowed_claims: Independent review found no P0 or P1 defect in the bound V5 scalar numerical reference implementation.
The V5 exact-dyadic local-driving implementation repairs the registered V4 plus/minus 2^-104 sign-loss defect for the reviewed registered and independent mutations.
For reviewed inputs, local D returns a finite correctly signed binary64 value, a proved positive zero for exact equality, or BaiReferenceError; no exact nonzero was silently reported as zero.
The bound V5 source may be used as a scoped Bai scalar coefficient/root regression reference implementation baseline for later tolerance and HCP-reduction gates.
